encounters.cc: Difficult-to-control hypertension despite three antihypertensive medications

lines: Difficult-to-control hypertension despite three antihypertensive medications
She was diagnosed with high blood pressure 12 years ago and had stable control for many years on a low-dose thiazide.
Over the past 8 months, however, her blood pressure has progressively worsened despite the addition of an ACE inhibitor and calcium channel blocker.
She now takes 3 antihypertensive medications at maximum doses but continues to have systolic readings >160 mm Hg at home.
She also reports cramping pain in both calves that starts after walking 2–3 blocks and resolves within minutes of rest.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
Her medical history includes type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and a 40-pack-year smoking history.
She quit smoking last year after developing transient dizziness while walking uphill.
She denies chest pain, dyspnea, or syncope.
On physical exam, her BMI is 23 kg/m² and her blood pressure is 170/100 mm Hg in the right arm and 140/90 mm Hg in the left arm.
Her radial and brachial pulses are symmetric and full, but femoral and dorsalis pedis pulses are decreased bilaterally.
Auscultation reveals a soft abdominal bruit in the right periumbilical area.
Funduscopic exam shows mild arteriolar narrowing but no hemorrhages or exudates.
She has trace pretibial edema but no signs of heart failure.
Her lower extremities show cool skin and diminished hair growth below the knees.
The rest of the exam is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping for six months following husband's death

lines: Persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping for six months following husband's death

The patient is a 66-year-old female with hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, chronic insomnia, and recurrent ischemic stroke who returns to clinic following her recent Internal Medicine evaluation for renal artery stenosis.
She reports a 6-month history of persistent sadness, loss of interest in activities, and difficulty sleeping.
She reports a 15-pound weight loss during this period.
Her husband passed away 8 months ago, and since then, she has felt "empty" and has been isolating herself from friends and family.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 1 year ago, 40 pack-year history.
Appears fatigued and has poor eye contact

encounters.cc: Two months of increasing pain and stiffness in neck, shoulders, and hips, worse in the mornings

lines: Two months of increasing pain and stiffness in neck, shoulders, and hips, worse in the mornings
The patient with renal artery stenosis and recurrent stroke presents with two months of neck, shoulder, and hip pain and stiffness.
She reports that symptoms are worse in the mornings and after periods of inactivity, but improve slightly with movement.
She also mentions experiencing mild fatigue and a 4-pound unintentional weight loss.
She has no history of joint swelling.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 1 year ago, 40 pack-year history.
On physical examination, there is no joint swelling or tenderness, but there is a decreased range of motion in the shoulders and hips due to pain.
- Complete blood count (CBC): Within normal limits

encounters.cc: Admitted with acute cholecystitis; surgical evaluation after 48 hours of intravenous antibiotics

lines: Admitted with acute cholecystitis; surgical evaluation after 48 hours of intravenous antibiotics
The patient is a 68-year-old female with history of renal artery stenosis, major depressive disorder, and polymyalgia rheumatica who is admitted for surgical evaluation.
After 48 hours of intravenous antibiotics, the surgical team recommends a laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
She has a history of hypertension and well-controlled type 2 diabetes.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 1 year ago, 40 pack-year history.
The patient is alert, oriented, and speaks fluently.
When the surgeon enters the room to discuss the procedure, the patient’s daughter insists on being present and states, “My mother always gets confused when doctors talk.
Just explain everything to me, and I’ll decide for her.” The physician politely asks the daughter to leave so he can speak directly to the patient.
The patient agrees and listens carefully.
She asks appropriate questions about risks and benefits and ultimately consents to the procedure.
The daughter later files a complaint, claiming the physician ignored the family’s right to be involved in decision-making.

encounters.cc: Follow-up visit after recent hospitalization for lacunar stroke with residual left-sided weakness

lines: Follow-up visit after recent hospitalization for lacunar stroke with residual left-sided weakness
The patient returns for follow-up after stroke hospitalization.
She has been experiencing mild left-sided weakness and difficulty with coordination since the event.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
Her current medications include metoprolol, lisinopril, and metformin.

Her daughter pulls you aside and requests that you do not disclose any findings that might suggest a progressive or debilitating disease, as she fears this will cause her mother undue stress and despair.
On examination, her blood pressure is 132/86 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm
She has a mild left-sided hemiparesis
Her laboratory values are as follows:
The patient's recent MRI showed a small, chronic right lacunar infarct.

encounters.cc: Persistent sadness, lack of interest in activities, and fatigue for three months since the stroke

lines: Persistent sadness, lack of interest in activities, and fatigue for three months since the stroke
The patient with history of recurrent ischemic stroke and prior depression presents to the clinic with her daughter three months following her recent lacunar stroke.
The daughter reports that her mother has been experiencing persistent sadness, lack of interest in activities, and fatigue for the past three months.
She denies any recent changes in medication, diet, or physical activity.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
The patient had an ischemic stroke six months ago, which resulted in mild right-sided weakness.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Her current medications include lisinopril, metformin, and aspirin.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 1 year ago, 40 pack-year history.
Her blood pressure is 132/86 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, and BMI is 29 kg/m^2.
On examination, the patient has a flat affect and admits to feelings of hopelessness and occasional thoughts that life is not worth living.
Neurological examination shows mild right-sided hemiparesis.

encounters.cc: Severe right eye pain, headache, nausea, and blurred vision with halos around lights for four hours

lines: Severe right eye pain, headache, nausea, and blurred vision with halos around lights for four hours
This 70-year-old with hyperopia and stroke presents with eye pain.
She describes the pain as throbbing and states that it has progressively worsened.
She also reports blurred vision and halos around lights.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
Her past medical history includes hypertension and hyperopia.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 1 year ago, 40 pack-year history.
On physical examination, her right eye is red, the cornea appears cloudy, and the pupil is mid-dilated and non-reactive to light.
Visual acuity is decreased in the affected eye.
The intraocular pressure (IOP) of the right eye is measured at 48 mmHg, while the left eye has an IOP of 16 mmHg.

encounters.cc: Acute onset confusion and unsteadiness on feet over the past two days

lines: Acute onset confusion and unsteadiness on feet over the past two days

This 70-year-old with recurrent stroke and chronic insomnia on temazepam is brought to the emergency department by her daughter because of increasing confusion and unsteadiness on her feet over the past two days.
- History of recurrent ischemic stroke with residual mild bilateral weakness
The patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and chronic insomnia.
Her current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and a nightly temazepam that was prescribed 3 weeks ago.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 1 year ago, 40 pack-year history.
Her blood pressure is 145/85 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and random blood glucose is 180 mg/dL.
On examination, the patient is alert but oriented to person only.
She has a slow, shuffling gait and uses the wall for support.
There is no evidence of head trauma, and her neurological examination is nonfocal.
